AI Health Score Insights
Analysis across 2,847 active properties
✓ Good (Score 60+) — 68% of properties
Top reasons for high scores: Up-to-date HVAC servicing, completed roof inspections within 3 years, active warranties on major appliances, and consistent document uploads.
Individual actions: Keep maintenance reminders on schedule; ensure all warranties are uploaded.
Group action: Offer a community-wide HVAC tune-up deal through the marketplace to maintain these scores.
⚠ Fair (Score 40–60) — 24% of properties
Common issues: Overdue plumbing inspections (avg. 4.2 years), missing electrical panel documentation, and no recorded gutter cleaning in 18+ months.
Individual actions: Send targeted reminders for plumbing check-ups; prompt document upload for missing permits.
Group action: Launch a "Fair to Good" push — batch outreach with discounted inspector packages or pre-scheduled contractor visits.
✗ Poor (Score <40) — 8% of properties
Primary causes: No maintenance activity logged in 12+ months, missing foundation or roof documentation, unresolved flagged issues, and inactive homeowner accounts.
Individual actions: Admin review and direct outreach to homeowners; flag for account manager follow-up.
Group action: Deploy re-engagement campaign with free HomeHub setup assist sessions and a 30-day improvement challenge with badge rewards.

Permissions Matrix

Role × resource access grid — enforced server-side in production

⚠ Prototype View — Not Yet Server-Enforced
ARCH: This matrix defines the intended access model for HomeHub's multi-tenant SaaS platform. In the prototype, some boundaries are UI-only. In production, every row in this matrix maps to a server-side middleware check using the pattern: requirePermission(role, resource, action).
SOC2 CC6.1: Access to system components is restricted based on user role. All elevation requires explicit grant.
✓ Full Access
R Read Only
OWN Own Data Only
✗ No Access
LIM Limited / Scoped
Resource 👑 SuperAdmin 🛡️ Platform Admin 💰 Finance 💼 AE 🎧 Support 🏠 Homeowner 🔧 Contractor 📋 Inspector 🏘️ HOA 🏗️ Builder 🤝 NP Partner 🏢 Agency
ARCH Notes: QR code access is logged per-scan, scoped to specific property, and revocable by homeowner at any time. Contractor data access is strictly job-scoped — no browsing of homeowner profile or other jobs. HOA can see properties in their community but not individual homeowner financial data. Agency can see aggregate agent performance but not individual agent-client details without agent consent. NP Partners see only their own allocated giveback totals — never individual user data.

Audit Log

Security-relevant event history — immutable record

ARCH: In production, audit_logs are append-only (INSERT only, no UPDATE/DELETE allowed on this table). Every event includes: event_type, actor_id, actor_role, target_id, target_type, action, ip_address, user_agent, timestamp (UTC), session_id. Logs are replicated to cold storage within 24h. Retention: 2 years minimum for SOC2.

Maintenance Mode
Platform Maintenance Mode
All user-facing requests return a maintenance page. Admin access preserved.
OFF — Platform Live
ARCH: Maintenance mode sets a global Redis flag checked by the API gateway on every request. Cannot be enabled from this prototype.
Environment & Secrets
ARCH: Environment variables and secrets are NEVER stored in the codebase or localStorage. Use a secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, or Doppler) for: DB credentials, Stripe API keys, JWT secrets, S3/storage keys, email API keys, webhook secrets. Prototype uses placeholder values only — no real credentials in this file.

Impersonate User

Debug as any user — every session is logged to SuperAdmin audit trail

⚠ SuperAdmin Only. Impersonation creates an immutable audit log entry: impersonator_id, target_user_id, started_at, ended_at, actions_taken. Impersonated sessions are visually flagged (banner shown) and logged separately. Impersonation cannot be used to change another SuperAdmin's credentials or access settings.

Platform Intelligence Summary

Generated May 22, 2026 · Based on platform data from the last 30 days · Refresh weekly
📊 Executive Summary
HomeHub is in a strong growth phase with 14.2% MAU growth month-over-month. Contractor subscription revenue is the fastest-growing segment at +22%, driven by the PriceMatch v2 launch. Homeowner engagement is up significantly with avg session length increasing from 19 to 24 minutes. Three regions (Bay Area, Miami, Austin) account for 61% of new signups. The platform is on track to reach 5,000 MAU by Q3 2026 if current trends hold.
🏆 Wins This Month
Contractor Growth: 22% MoM increase in contractor subscriptions — highest ever. Driven by PriceMatch v2 referral loop.
RE Agency Momentum: 31% growth in agency subscriptions, with Coastal Realty Group being the largest-ever agency signup ($1,490/mo).
Session Engagement: Avg session up 26% (19→24 min). Document upload actions up 41%, indicating users are actively using HomeHub as their home OS.
Giveback Impact: $4,728 allocated this month to NP partners. Habitat for Humanity SF reported this drives referrals — 14% of new homeowner signups attributed to NP partners.
⚠️ Concerns & Watch Items
Inspector Segment Underperforming: 87 active inspector subscribers generating only $438/mo. Average session length is 9 min vs. 24 min platform avg. May indicate low feature discovery.
HOA Churn Risk: 2 HOA communities (280 combined homes) have not logged in for 45+ days. At-risk of churn at next renewal cycle.
Geographic Concentration: 61% of signups from 3 metros. Any regional economic downturn (especially SF Bay Area) creates disproportionate revenue risk.
💡 Recommendations
Inspector Feature Blitz: Run a targeted onboarding email sequence for inspectors highlighting Setup Assist + report integration. Goal: increase avg session to 18 min within 60 days.
HOA Re-engagement: Assign AE to the 2 at-risk HOA accounts for personal outreach. Offer complimentary setup assist session to demonstrate value before renewal.
Geographic Diversification: Prioritize Chicago, Denver, and Seattle for next AE hiring cycle. Current 3-metro concentration is a risk factor for Series A diligence.
PriceMatch Referral Loop: Contractor referral is now the #1 growth lever. Consider formalizing a referral program with a 1-month credit incentive to amplify this effect.
